definition: Shots attempted plus turnovers committed, from the official player box score, summed over the player's eligible games.
interpretation: How many offensive opportunities this player personally consumed. A VOLUME measure: it says nothing about whether the opportunities were used well.
eligibility: all 228 players in the 50 league-analytics-eligible completed games; all-star game and ASE/ASW squads excluded; no player is dropped for sample size
known_limitations: Shots reconcile exactly to team totals (4,106 in 100/100 team-games) but player-attributed turnovers total 1,369 against an official team total of 1,699 -- about 19% of league turnovers name only a team, so every player's count is understated. Assists and ground balls are deliberately excluded (an assist attaches to a goal already counted as the shooter's shot; 1,095 of 3,091 ground balls follow a faceoff). This is an INDIVIDUAL RECORDED opportunity count, not possessions played.

definition: recorded_offensive_opportunities divided by the same quantity summed over the player's team in the games he actually played.
interpretation: The share of his team's measurable offensive workload the player took on while he was available. The primary Phase 7 usage measure.
denominator: team shots + turnovers over the same games
position_adjustment: none -- this is the quantity that positional baselines are computed FOR
eligibility: all 228 players in the 50 league-analytics-eligible completed games; all-star game and ASE/ASW squads excluded; no player is dropped for sample size
known_limitations: NOT the share of team possessions the player was on the field for -- the PLL feed has no lineup, substitution or minutes data of any kind, so on-field participation is not computable. Because the denominator is games played, these do not sum to 1 within a team; offensive_play_share_season does. Inherits the ~19% turnover attribution gap.

definition: recorded_offensive_opportunities divided by the team's full-season total, summed over each team a mid-season mover played for.
interpretation: The same usage concept on a denominator that makes the shares add up: summing this over a team's players gives exactly 1.000.
eligibility: all 228 players in the 50 league-analytics-eligible completed games; all-star game and ASE/ASW squads excluded; no player is dropped for sample size
known_limitations: Penalises missed games by construction: a player who played 8 of 13 games looks low-usage even if he dominated the ball while available. Use offensive_play_share for the usage question and this one for the accounting check.

definition: The number of times the player appears anywhere in the eligible play-by-play log, in any role (shooter, faceoff winner or loser, ground-ball recoverer, penalty committer, pre-shot passer, or goalie of record on a shot).
interpretation: A faithful reproduction of the one usage definition Lacrosse Reference publishes. Reproduced for comparison; NOT this project's usage measure.
eligibility: all 228 players in the 50 league-analytics-eligible completed games; all-star game and ASE/ASW squads excluded; no player is dropped for sample size
known_limitations: Identical to Phase 6's play_shares column (validation check 5 asserts equality). NOT comparable across positions: per game it is 38.0 for faceoff specialists, 27.4 for goalies, 8.8 for attack and 2.5 for defense, because a goalie earns one appearance per shot he faces and a faceoff generates up to three (winner, loser, scrum recovery). It also contains the feed's unreliable shotAssistId pre-shot-pass indicator (1,791 appearances), which every Phase 6 value component deliberately excludes. Turnovers contribute ZERO appearances because the feed's turnover events name only a team.

definition: Official box-score touches divided by team touches over the games played.
interpretation: A broader involvement measure than offensive_play_share, including defensive and clearing touches.
eligibility: all 228 players in the 50 league-analytics-eligible completed games; all-star game and ASE/ASW squads excluded; no player is dropped for sample size
known_limitations: Player touch sums reconcile to team totals within 1.2% but match exactly in only 4 of 100 team-games. Counts a defenseman's clear and an attackman's dodge as the same unit, which is why it is a cross-check rather than the primary measure.

definition: offensive_EPA_points_raw (shooting_value + turnover_value) divided by recorded_offensive_opportunities.
interpretation: Value produced per offensive opportunity consumed. Pure efficiency, blind to volume.
baseline: 0 = a league-average outcome on those opportunities
eligibility: all 228 players in the 50 league-analytics-eligible completed games; all-star game and ASE/ASW squads excluded; no player is dropped for sample size
known_limitations: Dominated by sampling noise at low volume: at 13 opportunities the null standard error is roughly 0.13 EPA_points per opportunity, which is larger than almost any real between-player difference. Always read with the opportunity count beside it.

definition: EPA_points_raw divided by event_log_play_shares -- Lacrosse Reference's published usage adjustment ('you just divide total EGA by play shares') applied to this project's estimand.
interpretation: Reference reproduction only. Production per event-log appearance.
baseline: 0 = league-average outcomes on the player's own opportunities
eligibility: Lacrosse Reference applies a 1% team play-share minimum; reproduced here as future_award_input_eligible
known_limitations: The denominator is not comparable across positions (see event_log_play_shares), so this ratio is not a cross-position ranking. Identical to Phase 6's total_player_value_per_play_share. Lacrosse Reference's EGA is a different estimand from EPA_points, so this reproduces their OPERATION, not their METRIC.

definition: Fitted E[offensive_EPA_points_raw | offensive_play_share], from a mean function chosen among {constant, linear, quadratic} by 5-fold cross-validated MSE, fitted on field players with at least one recorded offensive opportunity.
interpretation: What a typical player at this usage level produced in 2026.
baseline: league fit over the field-player population
position_adjustment: the fit is a league fit, not a positional one; positional context is supplied separately by the *_position_* columns
reliability_method: 5-fold cross-validated MSE against a constant null
eligibility: NULL for goalies and faceoff specialists: they are outside the fitted population and no offensive-usage expectation is defined for them
known_limitations: The selected model in 2026 is the CONSTANT: usage has essentially no cross-validated predictive power for total offensive EPA (Pearson r = +0.03 among offensive field players). Subtracting this expectation therefore does very little, which is itself the finding -- what usage changes is the VARIANCE of value, not its mean. Fitted on a single season of 228 players and not validated on held-out seasons.

definition: offensive_EPA_points_raw minus expected_EPA_given_usage.
interpretation: How much more or less value the player produced than a typical player at his share of team offensive opportunities.
position_adjustment: none directly; positional versions are the *_position_* columns
eligibility: field players with opportunities
known_limitations: Because the selected mean function is a constant, this residual is offensive EPA minus a single league number and carries all the same limitations. It is NOT a per-opportunity measure and a high-volume player can post a large residual on ordinary efficiency.

definition: EPA_vs_usage_expectation divided by offensive_EPA_null_sd -- the residual expressed in units of the sampling spread at the player's own opportunity volume.
interpretation: How unusual the player's production is given how many chances he actually had. A value of +2 means his season is about two chance-standard-deviations above the usage expectation.
unit: standard deviations of the chance distribution
baseline: the usage expectation, scaled by chance variation
position_adjustment: volume-adjusted, not position-adjusted; the two are separate columns
reliability_method: closed-form binomial/Poisson sampling variance of the component
eligibility: field players with opportunities
known_limitations: Not a p-value and not a skill estimate. It measures distance from chance, so a player who genuinely is better than average SHOULD score above zero; it does not shrink toward the mean and must not be read as an estimate of underlying ability. The normal approximation implied by reading it as a z-score degrades below roughly 20 opportunities.

definition: The standard deviation EPA_points_raw would have under chance alone at the player's own opportunity counts: sqrt of the sum of the closed-form sampling variances of every component that applies to him.
interpretation: The size of the swing this player's season could show through luck alone. The scale against which any claim of unusual performance has to be judged.
baseline: league-average conversion on the player's own opportunities
position_adjustment: none -- this is a per-player, volume-driven quantity, not a positional one
reliability_method: closed form: one-point attempts p(1-p); two-point attempts 4p(1-p); turnovers and faceoffs binomial scaled by their coefficients; caused turnovers Poisson
eligibility: all 228 players in the 50 league-analytics-eligible completed games; all-star game and ASE/ASW squads excluded; no player is dropped for sample size
source_columns: one_point_attempts, two_point_attempts, touches, faceoffs, shots_on_goal_faced, games_played
known_limitations: Assumes opportunity outcomes are independent, which shots within a game are not exactly. Uses the league conversion rate rather than the player's own, so it is the null spread, not the spread around the player's true ability. The caused-turnover term is a Poisson approximation because the feed provides no caused-turnover denominator.

definition: The player's rostered position, resolved once per player as the modal non-null box-score label (ties broken alphabetically) and mapped to a spelled-out name.
interpretation: What the player is listed as. Not what he measurably did -- that is value_role.
eligibility: all 228 players in the 50 league-analytics-eligible completed games; all-star game and ASE/ASW squads excluded; no player is dropped for sample size
known_limitations: Two of 228 players carry no label in any game and are mapped 'unknown' rather than guessed. PLL labels are role-specific and map one-to-one; no NCAA convention is assumed. Resolution is deterministic and reproduces exactly on a rerun.

definition: Analytical role derived from measured opportunity: goalie if the player faced any shot on goal as goalie of record; faceoff if he took at least 50% of his team's faceoffs in the games he played; otherwise offensive_field or defensive_field BY ROSTER POSITION.
interpretation: What the player measurably did, where the data can tell -- used to choose which baseline, which reliability rate and which caveat applies to him.
eligibility: all 228 players in the 50 league-analytics-eligible completed games; all-star game and ASE/ASW squads excluded; no player is dropped for sample size
known_limitations: The offensive/defensive split is NOT measured -- it falls back to the roster label, because the feed attributes exactly one defensive act (caused turnovers, 741 league-wide against 4,106 shots), and an opportunity-share rule put 24 of 96 rostered defenders in the offensive class. Lacrosse Reference's documented classifier uses shares of VALUE; that cannot be applied to EPA_points, which is a signed residual, so opportunity shares are used and the divergence is documented.

definition: The player's mid-rank empirical-CDF percentile of EPA_points_raw within his position_group, on 0-100.
interpretation: How unusual the player's season was among players with the same roster role. The recommended positional comparison, because it assumes nothing about the distribution.
reliability_method: none -- a rank carries no interval
eligibility: all 228 players in the 50 league-analytics-eligible completed games; all-star game and ASE/ASW squads excluded; no player is dropped for sample size
known_limitations: Coarse in a small group: 13 faceoff specialists means 7.7 percentile points between adjacent players. Compares totals, so it rewards opportunity volume within the group as well as quality. A percentile is NOT comparable across position groups -- the 90th percentile goalie and the 90th percentile attackman are not equally valuable.

definition: (EPA_points_raw - position_group mean) / position_group standard deviation.
interpretation: The same comparison as the percentile, on a standard-deviation scale.
reliability_method: the group sd's own relative standard error is published as relative_se_of_sd in player_positional_baselines.csv
eligibility: NULL where the group has fewer than 9 players with the metric
known_limitations: Assumes an approximately symmetric group distribution, which is only partly true here: offensive_field EPA_points is right-skewed (+0.75) and defensive_field shooting value has excess kurtosis +3.4. Prefer the percentile or the robust z. Suppressed for the 2-player 'unknown' group.

definition: (EPA_points_raw - position_group median) / (1.4826 x position_group median absolute deviation).
interpretation: A standard-deviation-scaled positional comparison whose denominator a single outlier cannot set.
eligibility: NULL where the group has fewer than 9 players with the metric
known_limitations: The 1.4826 factor matches a normal sd, so this and the ordinary z coincide under normality and diverge exactly where the ordinary z should not be trusted. Still a within-group comparison and still not cross-position comparable.

definition: n / (n + kappa) where n is the player's shot attempts and kappa is the empirical-Bayes beta prior strength estimated from the league by method of moments.
interpretation: The weight the posterior places on the player's own record rather than the league prior. 0.5 means his own shooting is exactly as informative as the assumption that he is league-average.
baseline: the league's estimated prior strength (70.8 attempts in 2026)
position_adjustment: none -- reliability is a property of the player's sample, not his position
shrinkage_method: empirical-Bayes beta-binomial (Phase 6's estimator, imported not re-derived)
reliability_method: posterior weight; exact 95% beta-posterior interval published alongside
eligibility: NULL for players with no shot attempts
known_limitations: In 2026 only 13 of 192 shooters reach reliability 0.5, i.e. 71 attempts. Shooting ability is weakly identified in a 13-game season and rate leaderboards should be read with that in mind.

definition: n / (n + kappa) for faceoff win percentage; kappa = 15.9 draws in 2026.
interpretation: The best-identified rate in the framework. 18 of 47 players who took a draw reach 0.5.
baseline: the league's estimated prior strength (15.9 draws)
eligibility: NULL for players who took no faceoffs
known_limitations: A weak prior means real between-player differences exist and are detectable, not that any individual estimate is precise. No opponent adjustment: a specialist who happened to face weaker opposing specialists is not discounted.

definition: n / (n + kappa) for save percentage; kappa = 300.3 shots on goal in 2026.
interpretation: How much of a goalie's save percentage is his own record rather than the league prior.
denominator: shots on goal faced + prior strength
baseline: the league's estimated prior strength (300.3 shots on goal)
eligibility: NULL for players who faced no shots on goal
known_limitations: Only 1 of 16 goalies reaches reliability 0.5 in 2026 -- the busiest goalie faced 309 shots on goal against a prior strength of 300. Save percentage is barely identified in a single PLL season. Compounded by the absence of any shot-quality adjustment.

definition: n / (n + kappa) for two-point conversion; kappa is capped at 1,000,000 because the observed between-player spread is SMALLER than binomial noise alone predicts.
interpretation: Effectively zero for every player. There is no measurable two-point shooting skill in the 2026 season.
baseline: a prior so strong that every player's shrunk rate is the league mean
eligibility: NULL for players with no two-point attempts
known_limitations: THE DATA CONTAIN NO EVIDENCE THAT PLAYERS DIFFER IN TWO-POINT SHOOTING ABILITY. The median player took 2 two-point attempts and the maximum was 29. No two-point rate leaderboard should be published from this season, and a test enforces that no such estimate is presented as reliable.

definition: TRUE when the player's reliability on the rate that drives his role's leaderboard (shooting for field players, faceoff win % for specialists, save % for goalies) is at least 0.5.
interpretation: Whether there is enough of the player's own record to rank him on a RATE. Players who fail it stay in the table with their observed production intact.
eligibility: all 228 players in the 50 league-analytics-eligible completed games; all-star game and ASE/ASW squads excluded; no player is dropped for sample size
known_limitations: 0.5 is the point at which a player's own record outweighs the league prior in the posterior -- a property of the estimator, not a round number. The trial count it implies differs per rate (16 draws, 71 shots, 300 shots on goal) because each prior is estimated separately. It is deliberately strict: 13 of 192 shooters and 1 of 16 goalies clear it in 2026.

definition: TRUE when the player accounts for at least 1% of his team's event-log play shares.
interpretation: Lacrosse Reference's own published minimum-usage cutoff, reproduced. An INPUT to a later phase's eligibility decision, not an award qualification.
eligibility: all 228 players in the 50 league-analytics-eligible completed games; all-star game and ASE/ASW squads excluded; no player is dropped for sample size
known_limitations: Adopted because it is documented rather than invented, but it inherits every defect of the event-log play-share measure: it is far easier for a goalie or a faceoff specialist to clear than for a rotational defenseman. It is NOT a statement that the player deserves award consideration; Phase 7 builds no award model.

definition: Always TRUE. Defensive value in this framework is caused turnovers above a positional per-game average, and nothing else.
interpretation: A permanent warning carried on every row so a defensive number can never be read as comprehensive.
eligibility: all 228 players in the 50 league-analytics-eligible completed games; all-star game and ASE/ASW squads excluded; no player is dropped for sample size
known_limitations: Positioning, matchup difficulty, forcing a bad shot instead of a turnover, sliding, communication and shot suppression leave no trace in this feed and are absent from the number. The denominator is games played, with no minutes or shifts available. A defensive value of 0 does NOT mean 'an average defender' -- it means 'caused turnovers at the positional per-game rate, with everything else unmeasured'.

definition: Always TRUE. Every usage measure here counts individually recorded actions.
interpretation: A permanent warning that no column in this phase is possession participation.
eligibility: all 228 players in the 50 league-analytics-eligible completed games; all-star game and ASE/ASW squads excluded; no player is dropped for sample size
known_limitations: Team possessions while a player was on the field cannot be computed from this feed: it carries no lineup, substitution, shift or minutes data. Nothing in Phase 7 is denominated in possessions or in time, and validation checks 21 and 22 enforce it.

definition: NOT SUPPORTED. Never computed.
interpretation: Named here so its absence is explicit rather than an omission a reader has to notice.
eligibility: not_applicable
known_limitations: The PLL feed has no lineup or on-field data of any kind. Any metric of the form 'share of team possessions while on the field' is unsupported and is not published under any name.
